industry.ev: Electric buses rose from 147 (FY19) to 4,993 (FY26); the company expects >30% EV penetration in buses by 2030. An electric bus or truck has no engine-driven compressor, so ZF sells e-compressors (Tata Motors localisation award, Sep-2026), EBS and ECAS; the content per EV is at least as high as per diesel vehicle. Electric trucks are still pilots.

Low of the year to 30-Sep-2026 (US tariffs hit exports)
Q1FY27: revenue +9.3%, PAT -14.7% (FX base), ESC nominations from three OEMs
Rs2,321 that week, then Rs2,637 by 7-Aug
moat: Incumbency in air brakes
Strong

Six decades as the supplier of record to Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, VECV, Daimler India and Mahindra (30+ customer awards in 12 years); the ZF group claims ~80% share in CV braking; ABS on every truck it supplies
Air-brake systems are safety-critical and validated per platform: OEMs rarely switch
Regulated content (ESC, ADAS)
Strong (ESC) / Unproven (ADAS)
Pneumatic ESC nominations from three major OEMs ('retaining our majority position'); full ADAS suite with two OEMs; own ESC test track
The Oct-2027 mandate is the next leg; AEBS/ADAS can be bought separately and 'there are many other players in the market' (Jul-2026)
Parent technology and global sourcing
Strong, but rented
WABCO/ZF products and R&D; royalty Rs101 cr (2.5% of revenue); 76% of goods exports go to ZF CV Systems Global at cost-plus prices
Access to technology and export volumes depends on the parent, which also sets the margin on exports
Aftermarket reach
Moderate-Strong
~550 dealers/distributors, ~270 service partners, 6,000+ retailers; aftermarket +15.6% in FY26 and Q1FY27
Spares on a large installed base: steady, higher-margin cash flow
Cost position
Moderate
EBITDA margin 15-16.5% (FY24-26) vs 18-20% for Sona or Schaeffler; aluminium ~18% of costs passed on with a lag; Q1FY27 12.9%
Pricing power with OEMs is real but slow
Engineering services to the group
Moderate
Rs504 cr of services (software, R&D, support) billed to ZF at cost plus a mark-up; 1,100+ engineers
Low-risk, low-margin annuity; volume depends on how much work ZF moves to India
critiques: Raw-material inflation and higher other expenses made Q1 operationally muted; growth rests on higher content per vehicle.
CV upcycle plus ADAS/ESC regulation justify 50x P/E; exports should outgrow the industry as the group sources more from India.
The FY27 outlook is 'flattish with maybe single-digit small growth'; management is cautious.
A third of revenue is with one sister company (ZF CV Systems Global) at cost-plus prices set within the group; shareholders approved up to Rs2,500 cr for FY27.
Exports are hostage to the US and European truck cycles and to tariffs: -11% in FY26 and still ~20% below two years ago.
The promoter has sold 15% of the company since 2024; further sales are an overhang.
Regulation-led pre-buying (as before BS-VI in 2020) could flatter FY28 and hurt FY29 truck volumes.
